conventions.java.reading: Code reading by the spec helper, not a verification verdict: conforms / diverges / unclear.
conventions.reachable trie: A trie obtained from new Trie() or new Trie(store) by put/delete/deleteRecursive (all nodes in memory).
conventions.canonical-parse reading: The reading that Trie.fromMessage should accept only encodings that toMessage can produce (fromMessage(m).toMessage() == m). No RSKIP states it; obligations using it are kind=ambiguity.
conventions.sanity: spec/sanity/ReproHints.jsh runs every reproducer hint marked 'Sanity run' against the real compiled classes; output in spec/sanity/ReproHints.out.

applicability_notes.RSKIP107: Status Draft (IPs/RSKIP107.md:5; README.md:118). No ConsensusRule for 107: rskj always serializes nodes in this format. Its node hash is consensus for the state root from RSKIP126 (ConsensusRule.java:41; reference.conf:28 rskip126 = wasabi100; config/main.conf:8 wasabi100 = 1591000; testnet/regtest wasabi100 = 0; co/rsk/db/StateRootHandler.java:41-52) and for tx/receipt roots (co/rsk/core/bc/BlockHashesHelper.java:22-29,76-83; before RSKIP126 those use getHashOrchid). The RSKIPs clone has no IPs/RSKIP126.md.
applicability_notes.RSKIP108: Status Draft (IPs/RSKIP108.md:5; README.md:119). No ConsensusRule; TrieKeyMapper applies the mapping unconditionally in the current code.
applicability_notes.RSKIP24: Status Adopted (IPs/RSKIP24.md:5, :23) with 'Parts of this document has been deprecated' (IPs/RSKIP24.md:29). Only its design goals and immutability statement are used.
applicability_notes.RSKIP64: Status Draft (IPs/RSKIP64.md:5). Implemented by MultiTrieStore/GarbageCollector, used only when blockchain.gc.enabled (reference.conf:110-114, default false; co/rsk/RskContext.java:1605-1607).

obligations.title: Account key layout
obligations.quote:
| 0x00
SHA3(account_addr)[0:9]
account_addr | rlp(nonce,amount,flags) | account state | ... Therefore we can build keys using a 80-bit hash prefix to keep the trie balanced and concatenate the key with the original key, to make it unique.
obligations.statement: For every 20-byte address a, TrieKeyMapper.getAccountKey(a) == 0x00 ++ keccak256(a)[0..10) ++ a (31 bytes).

java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict. DOMAIN_PREFIX 0x00, SECURE_KEY_SIZE 10, then the raw address.

obligations.reproducer_hint: Sanity run: getAccountKey(0x00..01) has length 31 and starts 00 1468288056310c82aa4c (spec/sanity/ReproHints.out, line KEY).
obligations.notes: The 10-byte prefix length relies on the 80-bit reading of RSKIP108; see TRIE-KEY-02.

obligations.title: Hash-prefix slice notation [0:9] / [0..9] vs 80 bits
obligations.quote:
| 0x00
SHA3(account_addr)[0:9]
account_addr | rlp(nonce,amount,flags) | account state | | 0x00
SHA3(account_addr)[0:9]
account_addr
0x00
SHA3(storage_address)[0..9] trimmed_storage_address | byte array | value at a storage cell | ... Therefore a 80-bit hash digest prefix is more than enough
obligations.statement: The hash prefix in account and storage keys is exactly 10 bytes: TrieKeyMapper.secureKeyPrefix(x).length == 10 and == keccak256(x)[0..10).

java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict. Readings: (a) [0:9] half-open = 9 bytes (72 bits); (b) inclusive 0..9 = 10 bytes (80 bits). The prose says 80 bits and 'account trie keys consuming only 30 bytes' (10+20), so (b); Java implements (b).

obligations.reproducer_hint: Compare secureKeyPrefix(addr).length (10) with the literal half-open reading (9).
obligations.notes: Record as a finding on the RSKIP text; Java follows the prose.

obligations.title: Key mapping is injective and kinds are disjoint
obligations.quote: concatenate the key with the original key, to make it unique
obligations.statement: Distinct (kind, address, slot) triples map to distinct keys: getAccountKey is injective; account keys (31 B), code keys (32 B, last byte 0x80), storage-prefix keys (32 B, last byte 0x00) and storage keys (43..74 B) never coincide; getAccountStorageKey(a,s) == getAccountStorageKey(a',s') implies a == a' and s == s'.

java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict. Address bytes are embedded verbatim; trim is injective on 32-byte words.

obligations.notes: Derived: uniqueness is the stated purpose of appending the original key.

obligations.title: RSKIP112 value type specifiers
obligations.quote:
The non-zero values in the trie are prefixed by the following type specifier as a single byte:

- A for account or contract
- S for contract storage cell
- R for contract storage trie root
- D for coDe (C is reserved in case contracts are assigned their own type specifier)

Specifiers are shown in ASCII.
obligations.statement: Every non-zero value stored in the Unitrie starts with one ASCII type byte: 'A' account, 'S' storage cell, 'R' storage root, 'D' code.

java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict. rskj stores raw values (account RLP, code bytes, stripped storage words, 0x01 placeholder) with no type byte.

obligations.reproducer_hint: Any account value read from a Java-built state trie does not start with 'A' (0x41).
obligations.applicability: RSKIP112 Draft (IPs/RSKIP112.md:5); not implemented in rskj, no ConsensusRule. Informational.
obligations.notes: Recorded so the matrix can mark it not-applicable (Draft, not activated) rather than silently dropping it.

Each key in the trie is split into the four parts:

obligations.title: VarInt encoding table
obligations.quote:
**Variable length integer**

Integer can be encoded depending on the represented value to save space. Longer numbers are encoded in little endian.

| Value          | Storage length | Format                                  |
| -------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| < 0xFD         | 1              | uint8_t                                 |
| <= 0xFFFF      | 3              | 0xFD followed by the length as uint16_t |
| <= 0xFFFF FFFF | 5              | 0xFE followed by the length as uint32_t |
| -              | 9              | 0xFF followed by the length as uint64_t |
obligations.statement: For 0 <= v < 2^64 (as unsigned), VarInt(v).encode() is: [v] if v < 0xFD; 0xFD ++ uint16LE(v) if v <= 0xFFFF; 0xFE ++ uint32LE(v) if v <= 0xFFFFFFFF; else 0xFF ++ uint64LE(v).

refs: co.rsk.bitcoinj.core.VarInt (bitcoinj-thin-0.14.4-rsk-18.jar, decompiled with javap -c: VarInt(long), VarInt(byte[],int), sizeOf, encode)
java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict. bitcoinj sizeOf/encode follow the table; negative Java longs are treated as 9-byte values.

We can use version number 0 for Orchid encoding, 1 for the current encoding (RSKIP107), and 2 for nodes with rent time stamp (current proposal).

obligations.title: Child presence/embedding flag bits
obligations.quote:
- **nodePresent**: 2 bits indicate left/right embedded node (bit 2 = left, bit 3 = right)
  - **nodeIsEmbedded**: 2 bits indicate left/right node presence (bit 0 = left, bit 1=right)
...

  - if  !nodeIsEmbedded[0]:
obligations.statement: The four low flag bits follow the RSKIP: presence of left/right and embedding of left/right at the bit positions the text assigns.

java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict. The text swaps names and descriptions (nodePresent is described as 'embedded', nodeIsEmbedded as 'presence'); the conditional layout at :64-75 uses nodePresent as presence. Reading A (by name): present L=bit2 R=bit3, embedded L=bit0 R=bit1. Reading B (by description): embedded L=bit2 R=bit3, present L=bit0 R=bit1. Java: present L=bit3 (0x08) R=bit2 (0x04), embedded L=bit1 (0x02) R=bit0 (0x01); this matches neither reading (it is reading A with left/right exchanged).

obligations.reproducer_hint: Sanity run: trie {00:01, 0000:02} root = 5a070004500600020401: flags 0x5a (version 0x40, prefix 0x10, left present 0x08, left embedded 0x02). Both RSKIP readings give 0x55 here (A: present-left bit2 0x04 + embedded-left bit0 0x01; B: present-left bit0 0x01 + embedded-left bit2 0x04). A left child referenced by hash separates A (0x04) from B (0x01); Java writes 0x08.

All values (of trie nodes) that are longer than 32 bytes are stored separately.
  - **valueHash**, 32 bytes: Hash digest of value stored
obligations.statement: After s.save(t), for every node with hasLongValue, s.retrieveValue(valueHash) == value and valueHash == keccak256(value).

java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict. Values share the node keyspace (comment :121-129).

obligations.title: Epoch stores: write newest, read newest to oldest
obligations.quote:
Any trie node added during execution must be written in the last created database without exception.
All new state data will be written to the last database created, while old data will be searched on the latest database, and if not found, on previous databases. Even if there is a blockchain reorganization, the database to start searching will be the last one created.
obligations.statement: MultiTrieStore.save/saveValue write only to the current epoch store; retrieve/retrieveValue return the entry from the newest epoch that has it.

java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict.

obligations.title: Epoch migration keeps live nodes
obligations.quote:
**Epoch migration process**. Given two consecutive epochs `A`, `B`, their frontier blocks `a`, `b`, and databases `d(A)`, `d(B)`, a new epoch `C` will be created, with frontier block `c` and database `d(c)`. Then

1. `d(C)` is considered the new database for new updates.
1. We take `s` the `state` at `b.`
1. We travel `s` searching the trie for all entries in `d(A)` but not in `d(B)`.
1. For each entry in `d(A)` and not in `d(B)`, the entry is copied into `d(B).` Children of copied nodes could be copied automatically without checking existence in d(B).
1. `d(A)` is deleted (atomically)
obligations.statement: After MultiTrieStore.collect(r), every node and long value reachable from root r is still retrievable (entries only in the oldest epoch are copied to the next one before it is disposed).

java.note: Code reading only, not a verification verdict. collect retrieves r (marked saved by retrieve, :94) and calls save on it; TrieStoreImpl.save returns at once for saved nodes and only walks loaded children, so nothing is copied.

obligations.reproducer_hint: Sanity run: MultiTrieStore(0, 3, TrieStoreImpl(HashMapDB) factory); save a 2-key trie; collect(root) three times; retrieve(root) is present after collects 1 and 2 and absent after collect 3.

obligations.title: treeSize supports verifiable chunked sync
obligations.quote: The value treeSize enables sharding the state tree between nodes and requesting pieces in parallel from different nodes by specifying and offset and size of the requested chunk, while still being able to validate each piece independently, without the need to collect all pieces first.
obligations.statement: A chunk of the serialized tree identified by (offset, size) can be verified against the root using treeSize values, without the other chunks.
